native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Accounting for academic characteristics changes the two background effects in opposite directions. In NLSY79, post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress (highest grade >= 13 by 1979, or dorm/fraternity/sorority residence in 1981-88; 19.8% of 12,532 respondents) is overwhelmingly predicted by family SES - each extra year of the better-educated parent's schooling raises the odds by a factor of 1.33 (95% CI 1.30-1.35; +33 percentage points comparing parents with <=8 versus >=16 years) - and adding parental education alone absorbs essentially all of the unadjusted racial gaps (Black -10.9pp, Hispanic -6.1pp, both reduced to about zero and non-significant). Adding 1981 ASVAB test scores then attenuates the SES effect by roughly a third of its log-odds (AOR 1.33 -> 1.18; -44% naive, -32% KHB scale-corrected, -53% of the average marginal effect; the parent-college advantage halves from +32pp to +17pp) while leaving it large and highly significant, whereas the race coefficients do not attenuate at all - they reverse: Black AOR 0.96 -> 1.59 and Hispanic 1.05 -> 3.20 (+5pp and +15pp adjusted risk differences). So academic characteristics account for a substantial share of the socioeconomic gradient but none of the racial gap: minority respondents with equal parental schooling and equal test scores were at least as likely as their non-black non-Hispanic peers to progress to post-secondary education. What survives adjustment as the real racial divide is unequal academic preparation (mean ASVAB composite at parent education 16+: NB NON-HISP +0.91, BLACK +0.51, HISPANIC +0.10 SD units), together with a race x SES interaction (Black x parent-ed AOR 0.80/yr, p<1e-6) showing the Black deficit widening at high parental education. The Hispanic advantage is the most robust single finding (ASVAB-adjusted AOR 2.6-3.3 on the composite outcome, 2.7-3.1 in the correctly temporally-ordered prospective variant, significant in every specification); the Black ASVAB-adjusted coefficient is much less stable (1.0-1.6 on the composite, 2.4-2.6 on the 1979-grade outcome, ~0.9 or below and statistically ambiguous on college residence and the prospective variant). This is a descriptive composition/decomposition, not a causal estimate: ASVAB and class rank are 1981 measures that partly post-date the 1979 attainment measure and are themselves socially patterned (r = 0.48 with parental education), and the outcome is observed post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress, not a completed degree.
native_result.WorkflowB: Read-only inspection then pre-registered analysis of data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61). Outcomes: y_O1 grade>=13 (1979); y_O2 dorm/frat/sorority 1981-88; y_O3 = y_O1 OR y_O2 (PRIMARY, 19.8%); y_PROSP = baseline grade<=12 -> dorm 1982-88 (prospective sensitivity). Code 95 in highest-grade treated as sentinel. SES = max(mother, father) years (linear, categorical <=11/12/13-15/16+, any-parent-BA); 1978 log income as sensitivity; 1985 signed log wealth exploratory and flagged as post-decision. Race = dummies vs NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC; sex and age1979 in every model from M1. Academic block = the four 1981 ASVAB scores re-standardised (columns are mislabelled 'Z'; actual mean ~476, SD ~100) or their composite; class-rank percentile = 1-(rank-0.5)/class size kept in a separate reduced-coverage model (55.6% missing). Ladder M0 -> M1 -> A (+SES) -> B (+academic) fitted for 4 outcomes x 15 specifications with statsmodels Logit (HC1) and OLS (HC1), average marginal effects, and KHB-style scale-corrected attenuation on identical samples (Var(y*) = Var(Xb_big) + pi^2/3; k = (pi/sqrt3)/sigma_small). Also: g-computed standardised race and SES risk differences, descriptive race x ASVAB and race x parental-education cross-tabs (2- and 3-way), missingness diagnostics and a missingness-mechanism logit, mean-imputation + indicator sensitivity, logit-vs-LPM sign/significance agreement audit, SES functional-form and race x SES interaction audit, and robustness checks (age dummies, single ASVAB scores, available-item mean, family size, age>=18, VIF). Deliverables: analysis/nls_analysis.py and 12 files in results/.
